name: Etapp 8: STF Såmmarlappa Fjällstuga - STF Tarrekaise Fjällstuga

officialSourceClaims.notes: Naturkartan gives the Såmmarlappa-Tarrekaise substage as 13 km while the grouped BD70 route is shown as 28 km.

distanceKm.confidence: high for official 13 km display; medium-high for approximately 11.6 km computed linework from both GPX and OSM

fieldReports: Roversmountains reported Såmmarlappa-Tarrekaise in about 3 hours 45 minutes in older conditions.
Wikiloc 2024 reverse track lists about 13.2 km for Tarrekaise-Sämmarlappa as part of a multi-day Padjelantaleden track.
Field reports warn that wet vegetation, old/new duckboards, Bádurgårsså side streams, and rocky/bouldery trail can slow the stage.

difficulty.description: No formal official difficulty grade found. Naturkartan describes the leg as short and flat but fairly strenuous because the path is rocky. Field reports add wet, muddy, boardwalk, side-stream, mosquito, and after-rain caveats.

routeType.directionForImport: Såmmarlappa/Sammarlappa to Tarrekaise, matching STF north-to-south section order
routeType.descriptionForApp: The stage continues south through Tarradalen from Såmmarlappa toward Tarrekaise. It is a short and mostly flat valley stage, but the walking can still be tiring because of stones, wet ground, long boardwalk sections, side streams, and dense birch vegetation. The route starts near the Tarraätno river, passes small bridges, sparse herb-rich birch forest, open wetland and heath, then reaches the Bádurgårsså ravine and alluvial fan where the Vaimok/Tarraälvshyddan side route leaves the Padjelantaleden. After the valley opens toward Tarraure, the stage ends at STF Tarrekaise on the lake's northern shore.

protectedArea.name: Pärlälvens fjällurskog nature reserve / Natura 2000, bordering Laponia to the north

rules.rule: No Pärlälven-specific dog ban was found, but the reserve is reindeer-herding land and loose dogs are restricted by reindeer and wildlife rules. Länsstyrelsen's 2026 notice says dogs in reindeer-herding areas must be leashed/enclosed where reindeer are present and herding is allowed; general wildlife rules restrict loose dogs 1 March-20 August. If a trip enters nearby Padjelanta/Sarek, the stricter national-park rule applies: leashed dogs only 1 January-30 April and otherwise prohibited.

The Pärlälvens reserve decision allows aircraft landing in the reserve and no Pärlälven-specific drone ban was found in this pass. Nearby Padjelanta/Sarek national parks are stricter and require County Administrative Board permission for drones and aircraft start/landing under current Laponia/Naturvårdsverket rules.
The whole reserve is year-round reindeer land with reindeer facilities. Avoid disturbing reindeer, avoid splitting herds, and do not camp by corrals or active herding facilities.

Fishing and hunting are allowed in Pärlälvens fjällurskog only under applicable laws and permits. Tarraure/Tarraätno waters require water-specific permit/rule checks before any app fishing context is published.

Even where reserve rules allow fires, county or local fire bans and real-time fire-risk decisions override normal practice. Check Länsstyrelsen, municipality/rescue service, Krisinformation and SMHI/Brandrisk Ute close to publication/departure.
rules.confidence: high for process; dynamic for current status

stageSpecificSafety.notes: Naturkartan describes the stage as short and flat but strenuous because the path is rocky. Field reports add wet/muddy sections, slick or deteriorated duckboards in older reports, and slow vegetation after rain.
Field reports describe Bádurgårsså as variable: easy or nearly dry in dry weather but potentially difficult after heavy rain. Small bridges and some fords/side streams are expected.

Pärlälvens fjällurskog can be periodically closed due to military activity; Länsstyrelsen says to contact Försvarsmakten. No stage-specific military closure was found on 2026-04-29, but this remains a must-check before publication/travel.

findings: Reported Såmmarlappa-Tarrekaise in about 3 hours 45 minutes.
After about 1 km, the path runs close to the river with many campsites, often used by fishers.
Later the trail stays farther from the main river through open birch forest.
About 3 km before Tarrekaise it crosses a broad gravel riverbed with little water in autumn.
Descent to Tarrekaise via Katabäcken can be very wet in rain.
Describes combined Såmmarlappa-Tarrekaise-Njunjes stage as 18.5 km.
Describes a good path along Tarraätno below the Tarrekaise massif, several small side-stream crossings, some bridged and some forded, normally easy.
Notes birch forest, river views, an extensive boulder/gravel field, Nordkalottleden/Vaimok-Pieskehaure junction, then Tarrekaise.
Reverse Njunjes-Tarrekaise-Såmmarlappa report says heavy rain made the Tarrekaise-Såmmarlappa half wet, muddy, leafy, and slow.
Some duckboards were decayed and some new duckboards appeared later.
Bádurgårsså was described as moody: nearly dry in dry weather but potentially impassable after heavy rain; on this day it required changing footwear but was passable.
conditionReports.confidence: high for older after-rain field conditions
